answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a mandatory interlocking contribution trellis: each agent must periodically dock at a public wharf and submit a unique solution that verifies against neighboring agents’ prior outputs, building toward a collective zenith of lattice integrity. Attackers cannot cheaply scale because every fake identity requires independent, non-shareable work that must interlock correctly with real peers; bulk farms fail when even one mismatched link collapses the chain, imposing real per-identity compute and coordination costs that grow with network size.
